sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the differences between Tishrei and Nissan, including that the drawing down in Tishrei is through arousal from below while in Nissan it is from above, and that Nissan is the source of miraculous, transcendent light.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing the distinction between Tishrei and Nissan in several matters.
And among them,
that the drawing down in Tishrei is through arousal from below,
and the drawing down in Nissan is from above,
an arousal from above of its own accord.
For this is that the blessing for rain is on Shemini Atzeret
(Tishrei)
and the blessing for dew is on Pesach
(Nissan),
for rain is
a drawing down through arousal from below, and dew is
that which descends from above by itself.
And there is another distinction between Nissan and Tishrei,
that the vitality drawn down on Rosh HaShanah
(Tishrei)
for the entire year is within boundary and measure
(which in general is the vitality that is invested within the creations in their inwardness),
which is the root of the conduct of nature,
and that Nissan is the head of the months
[for that it is called by the name "head of the months" is because from it vitality is drawn to all the months,
in the manner of a head in its simple sense, from which vitality is drawn to all the limbs of the body]
it is regarding the drawing down of the light of the boundless, which is above worlds,
the root of miraculous conduct that is above nature.
And this is that the creation of the world was in Tishrei and the Exodus from Egypt was in Nissan,
for the creation of the world is that the world was created measured and bounded according to the laws of nature,
and the Exodus from Egypt is the exit from the boundaries and limitations of the world through the revelation of the light of the boundless, which is above worlds.
And it can be said that these two matters are dependent on each other.
For the drawing down that comes through arousal from below
(the service of the created beings)
is measured and bounded according to the manner of the lower one,
and the drawing down that comes through arousal from above of its own accord is according to the manner of the upper one.
And based on this one must understand,
that the thought to create the world was in Nissan,
what is the connection of the creation of the world
(measurement and limitation)
to Nissan
(the revelation of the light of the boundless).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua regarding the time of the future redemption, linking it to whether redemption comes through repentance or through a revelation from above.

translations.translation: And behold, the dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua is also regarding the time of the future redemption.

For Rabbi Eliezer holds that in Nissan they were redeemed and in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed, and Rabbi Yehoshua holds that in Nissan they were redeemed and in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed.
And the Tzemach Tzedek explains
that they follow their respective views regarding the manner of the redemption.
For Rabbi Eliezer holds that if Israel repents they are redeemed, and if not, they are not redeemed,
therefore he holds that in Tishrei they are destined to be redeemed,
for then repentance is accepted with greater intensity.
For this, that the redemption of the Exodus from Egypt was in Nissan and the future redemption will be in Tishrei, is
because they differ in their manner.
For the redemption of the Exodus from Egypt was through the revelation from above,
and therefore it was in Nissan.
And the future redemption will be through repentance,
the service of Israel,
and therefore it will be in Tishrei.
[And this is also the reason for this, that the redemption of the Exodus from Egypt
(and likewise the redemptions that followed)
was a redemption after which there was exile,
the aspect of female,
and the future redemption will be an eternal redemption after which there is no exile,
the aspect of male,
for if a man emits seed first, a female is born,
[if] a woman emits seed first, a male is born].
And Rabbi Yehoshua holds, "Not with silver shall you be redeemed,"
not through repentance and good deeds
[for even if they do not repent they are redeemed],
therefore he holds that in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed.
And this, that the future redemption will be an eternal redemption,
the aspect of male,
even though the future redemption will also be through a revelation from above,
it is,
for the revelation of the future is from an exceedingly lofty place,
such that even when a man emits seed first, a male is born.
As it is written,
"And of Zion it shall be said, 'A man and a man was born in her,' and He, the Most High, will establish her."
For when the revelation is from an exceedingly lofty place,
and "He, the Most High, will establish her,"
then,
"A man and a man is born,"
for even when a man emits seed first, a man is born
(male).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section reconciles the two rulings that Israel is only redeemed through repentance and that they will be redeemed in Nissan, explaining that the repentance at the end of exile contains the power of the revelation from above.

translations.translation: And one must understand,
that regarding the manner of the redemption, the halachah follows Rabbi Eliezer,
as the Rambam wrote
that Israel is only redeemed through repentance,
and regarding the time of the redemption, it is brought in several discourses
that in the Midrash
it decided and ruled anonymously according to the view of Rabbi Yehoshua, that in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed.
And one can say the explanation of this,
based on what is said in Tanya,
that all the revelations of the future depend on our deeds and service during the time of exile.
For this matter is
(simply)
according to all opinions.
Except that according to Rabbi Yehoshua,
this, that through our deeds and service during the time of exile the revelations of the future will be drawn down,
is
(not from their own essence,
but rather)
because in our deeds and service during the time of exile there is the power of the revelation from above
(as will be explained in section 5).
And based on this, one can explain the reconciliation of these two rulings,
that Israel is only redeemed through repentance and that in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed,
for this, that Israel repents at the end of their exile and immediately they are redeemed,
is,
because in the performance of repentance by Israel at the end of their exile there is the power of the revelation from above,
the matter of Nissan.
